title: Correspondence between A.R. Luria and J. Piaget 1930–1966 years
abstract: The letters exchanged between the renowned 20th-century psychologists Aleksander Luria and Jean Piaget reveal the intricate and sensitive process of fostering collaboration between scholars from two distinct and frequently opposing social “camps”. The unseen participant (and probably the initiator) of these exchanges was Lev Vygotsky. This correspondence is being published for the first time. Notes by A.D. Maidansky and E. Yu. Zavershneva.
